title: The Elasticity of Substitution between Native and Immigrant Labor: A Meta-Analysis
abstract: arXiv:2609.26062v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper presents the first comprehensive meta-analysis of the elasticity of substitution between native and immigrant labor, drawing on 1,091 estimates from 41 studies. We find strong evidence of selective reporting: less precise estimates are systematically associated with lower reported elasticities. Correcting for this bias using meta-regression and selection methods raises the implied elasticity from about 13 to about 22, implying about 40% less relative-wage pressure from immigration than uncorrected results suggest. Bayesian and frequentist model averaging show that heterogeneity is driven mainly by geographic scale, data granularity, and whether the sample is restricted to low-experience workers, while the choice between log mean wages and mean log wages plays a secondary role. translated_title: 本土劳动力与移民劳动力之间的替代弹性：一项元分析
translated_abstract: 本文对本土劳动力与移民劳动力之间的替代弹性进行了首次全面的元分析，汇集了来自41项研究的1,091个估计值。我们发现了选择性报告的有力证据：精确度较低的估计值系统性地与较低的报告弹性相关。使用元回归和选择方法纠正这一偏差后，隐含的弹性从约13上升到约22，这意味着移民带来的相对工资压力比未经纠正的结果所显示的低约40%。贝叶斯和频率派模型平均方法表明，异质性主要由地理尺度、数据粒度以及样本是否仅限于低经验工人所驱动，而对数平均工资与平均对数工资之间的选择则起次要作用。我们的最佳实践估计值在剔除发表偏倚并优先使用最细粒度数据后，意味着基线地区层面的弹性约为17。
tldr: 本文通过首个针对本土与移民劳动力替代弹性的元分析发现，纠正选择性报告偏倚后弹性从约13升至约22（最佳估计约17），表明移民对本土工人相对工资的压力比以往研究显示的低约40%。
en_tdlr: This first comprehensive meta-analysis of the native-immigrant labor substitution elasticity finds that correcting for selective reporting bias raises the elasticity from about 13 to about 22 (best estimate ~17), implying roughly 40% less relative-wage pressure from immigration than previously estimated.
